rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi reads the passage as glad tidings that the Prophet’s preaching will spread through later generations and his present opponents will be routed until no one remembers them.
rows.anchor: This verse too gives glad tidings to the Prophet (sws) that the Almighty will cause his preaching mission to grow and spread

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is praised for success in this world and the next, with an unrivalled status in the world.
rows.anchor: The status he has achieved in this world was not achieved by anyone before.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s reward is not exclusive to Noah: He rewards anyone who conducts themselves with ih@sān, understood as obeying His directives with full sincerity.
rows.anchor: those who conduct themselves with ih@sān will be rewarded in this way by God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of Noah as a believing servant uses believer in its full sense: Noah truly believed.
rows.anchor: he indeed was among those of our people who well and truly believed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who claim faith and preach should emulate Noah; true belief means acting with ih@sān and brings the status he attained.
rows.anchor: they should try to follow this exemplary attitude

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God drowned those without ih@sān, sorting the worthy from the rest; sifting such people from creation is the world’s purpose, while the rest are cast into Hell.
rows.anchor: God will sift from it those who have this quality in them; the rest will be cast into Hell like waste material

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham belongs to Noah’s group: he and his followers continued Noah’s way, with the same call and the same faith and sincerity.
rows.anchor: he belongs to the same group and category as Noah (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All God’s prophets follow the same way, namely Islam.
rows.anchor: the way of all prophets of God is the same and that is the way of Islam

rows.speaker: Talmud
rows.claim: The Talmud says Noah instructed and trained Abraham.
rows.anchor: according to the Talmud, Abraham (sws) was instructed and trained by Noah (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi is not convinced by the Talmud’s claim, though accepts that it would further explain Abraham’s grouping with Noah if true.
rows.anchor: Though I am not convinced of this

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s pure heart was wholly free of polytheism and hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: refers to a heart which is totally free of the ailments of polytheism and hypocrisy

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sound heart has no shirk, hypocrisy, divided allegiance, or contamination; its love and obedience belong wholly to God, as the cited passage explains.
rows.anchor: their hearts will be free from all types of contamination and all their love and obedience will be for One God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking what they worship is a humiliating rebuke of their baseless objects of worship.
rows.anchor: he rebuked them by asking them what kind of baseless things they are worshipping

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ifk means something false and baseless; Abraham asks whether they wrongly pursue deities besides God.
rows.anchor: the verse actually means: do they falsely and wrongly go after other deities besides God?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question exposes the assumptions behind associating partners with God: that He lacks power, knowledge, justice, or mercy and needs helpers or intercessors.
rows.anchor: Are they under the false estimation that God alone is powerless to cater for their needs and to protect them?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only a deeply bad estimation of God could make someone tolerate partners; God’s honour means He will not tolerate interference in His being and kingdom and will cast alleged partners into Hell.
rows.anchor: On the contrary, He is powerful and strong and has a deep sense

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham spoke at an event in the place of worship; after the nighttime gathering ended, he looked at the stars to estimate the time and said he was tired so people would leave him there.
rows.anchor: when the event ended at night and people started to leave the place, he cast a glance on the stars as if he wanted to estimate the time

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once alone, Abraham secretly went to the idols, mocked their silence and inability to eat, then struck and smashed them.
rows.anchor: At first, he made sarcastic remarks before them: why are you not eating the food placed before you? And why are you so silent?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s glance at the stars was ordinary timekeeping, not belief in their intrinsic power or star-worship.
rows.anchor: It had nothing to do with

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an says Abraham smashed all the idols except the biggest; Sūrah Anbiyāʾ gives the reason for leaving it.
rows.anchor: At another place in the Qur’ān it is said that he smashed all except the biggest idol. Surah Anbiyā’ points out the reason for this.

rows.speaker: our exegetes
rows.claim: Exegetical narratives imply that Abraham lied and believed the stars had power in themselves.
rows.anchor: our exegetes, God knows why, have cited certain narratives while discussing this incident evident from which is that Abraham (sws) had lied on this occasion

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi rejects the narratives that make Abraham a liar or a believer in the stars’ intrinsic power, explaining his actions as innocent timekeeping and fatigue.
rows.anchor: superstition of star-worshippers or the powers of stars

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham used double-meaning words to stay overnight, leading the guards to believe he was too tired to go home.
rows.anchor: though he used double-meaning words to spend the night there as a result of which the guards were led to believe him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this festive context, Abraham meant he was tired and weak; using a double-meaning expression to stay overnight was not a lie or an evil belief.
rows.anchor: these words can in no way be considered as a lie or reflecting some evil belief

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guards understood that Abraham was weary and wanted to stay, considered the request harmless, and went home.
rows.anchor: They regarded this wish to be absolutely harmless; hence they did not interfere in it and leaving him alone went back to their homes.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal noun roghān means going somewhere secretly or furtively, indicating that Abraham moved after the guards had fallen asleep.
rows.anchor: The verbal noun روغان means to secretly and furtively go to or arrive at some place.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s jokes about the idols’ food and silence show that he was relaxed and delighted by the opportunity his successful plan provided.
rows.anchor: he was not worried at all; in fact, he was in a very jolly mood that he has been provided with a very opportune moment

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction implies that Abraham pounced on the idols to strike them; yamin denotes the right hand and here connotes a mighty blow.
rows.anchor: The word نیِمَی is used for the right hand, and since the blow struck by the right hand is hefty, here it is used to connote a mighty blow.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guards blamed Abraham because they had heard him censure the idols and warn that he would scheme against them.
rows.anchor: they cast the blame on Abraham (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham challenged the people to ask the idols what had happened; their inability to explain or avert it exposed their uselessness, and their confession that they could not speak led to his rebuke and their plot to burn him, which God thwarted.
rows.anchor: asked them to inquire from the idols what has struck them instead of inquiring from him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks how they can worship idols they carved from wood and stone when God created them, their materials, and the beings whose statues they make.
rows.anchor: you are the creators of your own creator; you should bear in mind that it is God who has created you as well as the wood and stones

rows.speaker: some scholastics
rows.claim: Some scholastics read “and what you make” as saying that God creates people’s deeds and actions.
rows.anchor: Some scholastics have argued that the words اَمَو َونُلَمْعَت refer to the fact that God is also the creator of the deeds and actions of people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi rejects that interpretation as contrary to the context; the verse concerns God’s creation of the idols’ makers and materials.
rows.anchor: This interpretation from the verse is absolutely against the context and occasion.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The temple authorities chose a covert plan to burn Abraham, perhaps to prevent his escape or interference from his family.
rows.anchor: instead of executing this plan openly, they tried to do it through a secret scheme

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s family could obstruct the plan because tribal support matters in these societies.
rows.anchor: In tribal societies, tribal support has great significance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exact scheme against Abraham cannot be determined from the Qur’an or Torah; Islahi infers that temple priests lured him to a great fire.
rows.anchor: It is difficult to answer what actual scheme they adopted against Abraham (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tribal stakes help explain the comparison: for a time the Quraysh also hesitated to attack Muhammad openly.
rows.anchor: the Quraysh were hesitant in openly adopting any aggression against Muh@ammad (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other Qur’anic passages show that Abraham was cast into the fire, but God protected him and the enemies’ plan failed.
rows.anchor: Abraham (sws) was cast into the fire but God’s power and mercy protected him from it and the scheme of his enemies was aborted.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After losing hope that his people would believe, Abraham decided to migrate, severing his ties with his environment for an uncertain new one and trusting God.
rows.anchor: Abraham (sws) lost hope in his people professing faith and decided to migrate from there.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording expresses Abraham’s confidence that God will guide him despite an unknown future, in keeping with God’s promise to guide those who strive for Him.
rows.anchor: The word ِنیِدْهَیَس reflects his confidence that though he does not know what the future has in store for him but he is hopeful that God will guide him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s prayer seeks righteous companions and supporters as well as offspring; pious children are the foremost members of such company.
rows.anchor: this prayer of Abraham (sws) does not merely relate to righteous offspring; it also relates to good companions and supporters

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi identifies the promised forbearing son as Ishmael.
rows.anchor: It is quite obvious that the son referred to here is Ishmael (sws).
